Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whilst my father (peace be upon him) and I were in the tawaf, a very tall man (sharjab) from among the men approached. I asked: 'What is a sharjab, may God set you right?' He said: 'A tall one.' He then said: 'Peace be upon you,'

and he inserted his head between me and my father. He said: So my father and I turned toward him and we returned his greeting. Then he said: 'I wish to ask you, may God have mercy on you.' My father said to him: 'We shall complete our tawaf, then you may ask me.' When my father completed the tawaf, we entered al-Hijr and prayed two rak'as. Then he turned and said: 'Where is the man, O my son?' And there he was, behind him, having already prayed.

He said: 'From where is the man?' He said: 'From the people of Syria.' He said: 'And from which of the people of Syria?' He said: 'From those who dwell in Jerusalem.' He said: 'Have you read the two Books?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Ask about whatever comes to you.'

So he said: 'I ask you about the origin of this House, and about His words: Nun, and the Pen and what they write [68:1], and about His words: And those in whose wealth there is a known right for the one who asks and for the deprived [70:24-25].'

He said: 'O brother of the people of Syria, hear our hadith and do not lie against us. For whoever lies against us in anything has lied against the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), and whoever lies against the Messenger of God has lied against God, and whoever lies against God, God the Mighty and Majestic will punish him.

As for the origin of this House: God, Blessed and Exalted, said to the Angels: I am going to place a vicegerent on earth [2:30]. The Angels responded to God the Mighty and Majestic, saying: Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood? So He turned away from them. They saw that as a sign of His anger, so they sought refuge at His Throne.

So God commanded an Angel from the Angels to build for Him a house in the sixth heaven, called al-Durrah, opposite His Throne. He designated it for the inhabitants of the heavens; seventy thousand Angels circumambulate it every day, never returning (again), and seeking forgiveness.

So when Adam descended to the lowest heaven, He commanded him with the restoration of this House, which is parallel to that (heavenly house). And He made it for Adam and his offspring, just as He had made that for the inhabitants of the heavens.' He said: 'You have spoken the truth, O son of the Messenger of God.'

key_terms.الحجر: Al-Hijr -- the semi-circular area adjacent to the Kaaba (Hijr Isma'il), where two rak'as are prayed after tawaf
key_terms.الشرجب: Sharjab -- an unusually tall person; a rare classical Arabic word glossed within the hadith itself
key_terms.الضراح: Al-Durrah (or al-Zurrah) -- the celestial Kaaba in the sixth heaven, visited by seventy thousand Angels daily
key_terms.الطواف: Tawaf -- the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba during Hajj and Umra
key_terms.الكتابين: The Two Books -- the Torah and the Gospel, indicating the questioner was a Jewish or Christian scholar
key_terms.بيت المقدس: Bayt al-Maqdis -- Jerusalem (the Holy House), indicating the man's religious background
key_terms.خليفة: Khalifa -- vicegerent, God's representative on earth; the Quranic term from 2:30

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the Kaaba according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a story in which he and his father Imam al-Baqir (AS) encountered a learned man from Syria during tawaf around the Kaaba. The Imam responded to his questions about the origin of the Kaaba, explaining its celestial counterpart al-Durrah in the sixth heaven, and how after Adam's descent to earth, God commanded him to restore the earthly House as a parallel act of worship for humanity. This hadith connects Quranic verses about creation and divine vicegerency to the cosmic significance of the Kaaba.
